main_body: Flat paving/floor patch of grey-brown stone slabs laid in a brick-like pattern with darker mortar joints (terrain tile, not a standing object)
top_band: none - ground surface seen from above, no standing top/front structure
evidence: Terrain paving patch. It is a flat top-down floor pattern with slab joints and small highlight chips, with no standing volume. Judged as terrain, the flat ground read is correct, and there is no object to fail the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: Each slab is a large flat fill of a single beige-grey (roughly 10x7 px or more) with no grain, speckle or per-stone shading. Only three tones appear: the slab, a mid-tone joint and a darker joint, plus a few lighter highlight chips at the top-left corners and small darker patches. The joints are a tinted dark version of the material, so outline is acceptable. The Beodeul paving reference has cobble texture, highlights on edges and many tones per tile. This candidate is much thinner and more regular, with tiles of about 2-4 colours, so it falls well below the standard.
